title: Projective GIT semistable replacement over a trait
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $r\geq2$, and $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$. Let $Z$ be a projective finite-type $k$-scheme [def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a $G$-action and an ample $G$-linearized invertible module $A$. Use the geometric semistability convention of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. Let $R$ be a discrete valuation $k$-algebra [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $z:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z^{ss}(A)$ be a morphism. There exist a DVR $R'$ with a local injective $k$-algebra map $R\to R'$, fraction field $K'$ finite over $K$, an element $h\in G(K')$, and a morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to Z^{ss}(A)$ whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K'$ is $h\cdot z_{K'}$. The map on spectra takes closed point to closed point. No characteristic-zero or linear-reductivity hypothesis is imposed. The scheme, invertible-module, projective and ample conventions are [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-invertible-module, def-kun-projective, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Section 3.3, proof of Corollary 11(2), printed p.17, semistable replacement (citing Mumford, Stability of projective varieties, Lemma 5.3). Arbitrary-characteristic projective GIT formulation; both local references WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-pgl-invariant-quotient] to obtain $q:Z^{ss}(A)\to Q$. The scheme $Q$ is proper over $k$, because it is projective. The generic quotient point $q\circ z:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Q$ therefore extends by the valuative existence criterion to $u:S=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Q$. Here $R$ is a valuation ring with its specified fraction field. Form $X=Z^{ss}(A)\times_Q S$; since $q$ is affine and of finite type, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for a finite-type $R$-algebra $B$. The point $z$ defines a $K$-point of the generic fibre of $X$.

source.place: Corollary 11(2), printed p.17: extension of the generic quotient point; expanded using projective quotient and valuative existence.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:G_K\to X_K$ be $g\mapsto g\cdot z$ and put $I=\ker(B\to K[G])$, $D=B/I$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset X$. The algebra $K[G]$ is a domain: $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,K}$ is the determinant-nonzero open in the projective space of matrices, hence is integral. Thus $D$ is a domain, $R\hookrightarrow D$, and $Y$ is an integral finite-type $S$-scheme dominating $S$. Its generic fibre is the reduced schematic closure of the orbit image. To verify invariance over the whole trait, write $H=R\otimes_k k[G]$. It is a free $R$-module, by choosing a $k$-basis of $k[G]$. The coaction of an element of $I$ maps to zero in $(D\otimes_RH)[1/\pi]$: write $\beta:B[1/\pi]\to K[G]$ for the orbit homomorphism. Equivariance says $(\beta\otimes1)\rho=\Delta\beta$, so it annihilates $I$. The injection $D[1/\pi]\hookrightarrow K[G]$ stays injective after tensoring over the field $K$; hence the image of $\rho(I)$ in $(D\otimes_RH)[1/\pi]$ is zero. Since $D\otimes_RH$ is a direct sum of copies of the torsion-free module $D$, localization at $\pi$ is injective. The coaction already vanishes in $D\otimes_RH$. Hence $I$ is preserved by the $G_S$-action and $Y$ is an invariant closed subscheme of $X$.

source.place: Agent coordinate expansion of the invariant orbit-closure construction before applying the universal closed-image property; group coaction identities and injectivity of localization on a torsion-free module.

proof.text: The universal closed-image clause of [lem-sfb-projective-pgl-invariant-quotient], with $T=S$ and $C=Y$, says that the image of $Y\to S$ is closed. It contains the generic point, since $\alpha$ factors through $Y_K$. The closure of that generic point is all of $S$, so $Y_s$ is nonempty. This applies to the actual base change along $u$, without any assertion that taking invariants commutes with this possibly nonflat base change.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(2), universal closedness, in the projective GIT example of the introduction, pp.490--491.

proof.text: The morphism $\alpha:G_K\to Y_K$ is a morphism of affine finite-type $K$-schemes. By [lem-wf-affine-constructible-open], its image is constructible and contains a nonempty open $U$ of its closure. The injection $D[1/\pi]\hookrightarrow K[G]$ shows that this closure is all of $Y_K$. Thus $U\subseteq Y_K$ is nonempty open and every point of $U$ has nonempty fibre under $\alpha$. This avoids requiring that a chosen lift of a quotient point belong to the original orbit.

source.place: Tag 054J, morphisms-lemma-chevalley; affine finite-type field case and dense constructible open consequence as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-generic-trait-selection] to $Y\to S$ and this $U$. Step 2 gives integrality, finite type and dominance, and Step 3 gives the required nonempty special fibre. We obtain $R\hookrightarrow R_0$, locally, with fraction field $K_0$ finite over $K$, and $c:\operatorname{Spec}R_0\to Y$ whose generic restriction is a point $y_0\in U(K_0)$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, more-morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X; its trait consequence in the cited node, using Tag 00PH.

proof.text: The fibre $G_K\times_{Y_K}\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ over $y_0$ is a nonempty affine finite-type $K_0$-scheme. Choose a maximal ideal of its nonzero coordinate ring; its residue field $K'$ is finite over $K_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. The resulting point is $h\in G(K')$ with $\alpha(h)=y_{0,K'}$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-domain-fg-field-dvr] to the Noetherian local domain $R_0$ and the finite, hence finitely generated, field extension $K'/K_0$. It gives a DVR $R'\subset K'$ dominating $R_0$ and with fraction field $K'$. Pull $c$ back along $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, then compose $Y\hookrightarrow X\to Z^{ss}(A)$ to obtain $b$. On the generic fibre the defining equality $\alpha(h)=y_{0,K'}$ is exactly $b_{K'}=h\cdot z_{K'}$. The composite $R\to R_0\to R'$ is injective and local; hence closed points map to closed points. The tower $K\subset K_0\subset K'$ is finite by multiplying vector-space bases. All maps are over $k$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-468cce468 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement in full. The item's statement is unchanged and it is still unsplit on live and side-live. Neither the item nor its via chain is on the 2026-10-19 drop list. The re-split note is for the parent, not this item. Step 1: the quotient gives a projective Q; Q is proper, and the valuative criterion over a valuation ring extends q∘z to S. X is affine over S. Step 2: I checked the scheme-theoretic invariance of I=ker(B→K[G]) through the coaction, flatness over K and torsion-freeness. That PGL_K is integral (it is D_+(det)) is elementary. Step 3: the closed-image clause with T=S and C=Y is a correct use of the node's statement and forces Y_s to be nonempty. Step 4: affine Chevalley, clause 2, gives a nonempty open U inside the orbit image. Step 5: all hypotheses of the trait-selection node hold. Step 6: Zariski's lemma, then 00PH via lem-sfb-local-domain-fg-field-dvr, give h∈G(K') and b with b_K'=h·z_K'. New node lem-sfb-projective-pgl-invariant-quotient is true by Alper Thms 9.1.4/9.7.6 and 5.3.1 (universal closedness of [Z^ss/G]→Q applied to the substack [C/G_T]); tested on a trivial action and on PGL2 acting on P^1 with O(2). New node lem-sfb-dense-generic-trait-selection is true by Stacks 05GU (more-morphisms l.14993) and 00PH (algebra l.29312): κ(z) is finite over K. Tested on R[x], on R[x]/(x²−π), where a degree-2 extension is needed, and on R[1/π], which the hypotheses exclude. Neither new node restates a clause of the item. I compared them with projective-pgl-stable-quotient (a stable-locus quotient only), pgl-geometric-reductivity, affine-pgl-finite-stabilizer-quotient, sbc-noetherian-specialization-trait and the local-domain DVR nodes: no duplicates. I accept the four declared tool uses (projective⇒proper, valuative existence, Chevalley, Zariski) as generic black boxes. Batch-5 flag: lem-sfb-local-domain-fg-field-dvr reaches sec-trace-formula only through def-trf-valuation-ring, a general Mathlib-leaf definition that plays no part in the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accept it. Minor point for the maintainer: the new nodes have no lean_audit field.

lean.note: Uses the general group-scheme linearization and PGL presentation exposed by the recorded Hilbert-Pluecker module. A point into the semistable open is represented equivalently by a point into Z whose image lies in U. The output DVR is identified with its image subalgebra in its fraction field, and the ring/field inclusions are explicitly compatible. No added characteristic or stabilizer restriction.
